epic.title: Watchlist & Price Alerts
epic.description: Allow retail investors to monitor price movements on securities they care about and receive timely notifications when target prices are crossed.
epic.businessValue: Increases 7-day active user rate from 22% to 31% by reducing the need for users to monitor competitor apps for price movements.

features.title: Watchlist Management
features.description: Users can build and manage a personal list of securities they want to monitor, with real-time quote data.

stories.title: Add a ticker to the watchlist
stories.goal: add any US equity or ETF ticker to my personal watchlist
stories.benefit: so that I can monitor securities I'm interested in without keeping a separate spreadsheet
acceptanceCriteria: Given I am on any ticker detail screen or search result, When I tap 'Add to Watchlist', Then the ticker appears on my Watchlist tab within 2 seconds and a confirmation toast is displayed
Given a ticker is already on my watchlist, When I tap 'Add to Watchlist', Then the button is replaced with 'In Watchlist' and no duplicate is added
Given I search for a ticker that does not exist (e.g. 'ZZZZZ'), When I tap search, Then an inline message 'Ticker not found' is shown and the Add to Watchlist button is not displayed

technical_notes.web_frontend: React component: <AddToWatchlistButton ticker={ticker} />. Use TanStack Query mutation (useMutation) for POST /api/v1/watchlist. Optimistic update: immediately add ticker to watchlist cache, rollback on error. Show toast via Radix Toast primitive (2s duration, bottom-right). Disable button during mutation (isLoading state). Handle 409 conflict by replacing button text with 'In Watchlist' (gray, non-interactive).
technical_notes.web_backend: .NET Minimal API: app.MapPost("/api/v1/watchlist", async (AddWatchlistRequest req, WatchlistService svc) => { ... }). Validate ticker exists by checking Redis cache (key: `ticker:{symbol}`, 24h TTL) populated from Polygon.io symbol list. Insert into watchlist_items table with UNIQUE constraint (user_id, ticker). Return 409 if duplicate detected at DB level. Use MediatR command: AddToWatchlistCommand. Return { ticker, sortOrder, addedAt } on success.

stories.title: View watchlist with live quotes
stories.goal: see the current price and intraday change for every security on my watchlist at a glance
stories.benefit: so that I can quickly assess whether anything needs my attention without opening each position individually
acceptanceCriteria: Given I am on the Watchlist tab with at least one item, When the screen is in foreground during market hours, Then each row displays the ticker, last price, and intraday % change updated within 15 seconds
Given the market is closed, When I view my watchlist, Then each row displays the previous close price and a 'Market Closed' label
Given my watchlist has no items, When I open the Watchlist tab, Then an empty state screen is shown with a 'Search for a ticker to add' call to action

technical_notes.web_frontend: React component: <WatchlistTable />. Fetch initial data via TanStack Query: useQuery({ queryKey: ['watchlist'], queryFn: fetchWatchlist }). Subscribe to live updates via SignalR connection: const connection = new HubConnectionBuilder().withUrl('/hubs/quotes').build(). Register handler: connection.on('QuoteUpdate', (update) => { queryClient.setQueryData(['watchlist'], (old) => old.map(item => item.ticker === update.ticker ? { ...item, ...update } : item)) }). Fallback: if WebSocket fails 3 times, switch to useQuery with refetchInterval: 15000. Empty state: render <EmptyState title='No tickers yet' action={<SearchButton />} /> if watchlist.length === 0. Market closed: check update.marketStatus === 'closed' and render badge.
technical_notes.web_backend: .NET SignalR Hub: public class QuotesHub : Hub { public async Task SubscribeToWatchlist(List<string> tickers) { foreach (var t in tickers) await Groups.AddToGroupAsync(Context.ConnectionId, $"quotes:{t}"); } }. Background service: QuoteIngestionWorker listens to Polygon.io WebSocket, publishes to Redis Pub/Sub channel `quotes:{ticker}`. Another worker (QuoteFanoutWorker) subscribes to Redis, publishes to SignalR via IHubContext<QuotesHub>.Clients.Group($"quotes:{ticker}").SendAsync("QuoteUpdate", payload). REST fallback: app.MapGet("/api/v1/watchlist", async (WatchlistService svc) => { var items = await svc.GetWatchlistAsync(userId); var quotes = await _quoteCache.GetManyAsync(items.Select(i => i.Ticker)); return items.Select(i => new { ...i, ...quotes[i.Ticker] }); });
technical_notes.database: -- No new tables needed. Quotes stored in Redis only (key: `quote:{ticker}`, value: JSON, TTL: 15s). Stale quotes trigger marketStatus: 'closed' in API response.

stories.title: Remove a ticker from the watchlist
stories.goal: remove a ticker I no longer want to follow
stories.benefit: so that my watchlist stays focused on my current interests
acceptanceCriteria: Given a ticker is on my watchlist, When I click the 'Remove' icon (trash) and confirm in the dialog, Then the row is removed immediately and any active alerts for that ticker are also deleted
Given I remove a ticker that has an active alert, When the removal is confirmed, Then I see a toast saying 'AAPL removed from watchlist. 1 alert deleted.'

technical_notes.web_frontend: React component: <WatchlistRow ticker={item.ticker} onRemove={handleRemove} />. Show Radix AlertDialog on trash icon click: <AlertDialog.Root><AlertDialog.Trigger asChild><IconButton icon={TrashIcon} /></AlertDialog.Trigger><AlertDialog.Content><AlertDialog.Title>Remove {ticker}?</AlertDialog.Title><AlertDialog.Description>This will also delete any active alerts.</AlertDialog.Description><AlertDialog.Action onClick={confirmRemove}>Remove</AlertDialog.Action></AlertDialog.Content></AlertDialog.Root>. Use TanStack Query mutation: useMutation({ mutationFn: (ticker) => api.delete(`/api/v1/watchlist/${ticker}`), onSuccess: (data) => { queryClient.invalidateQueries(['watchlist']); toast(`${data.ticker} removed. ${data.deletedAlerts} alert(s) deleted.`); } }). Optimistic update: filter out ticker from cache before API call.
technical_notes.web_backend: .NET Minimal API: app.MapDelete("/api/v1/watchlist/{ticker}", async (string ticker, WatchlistService svc) => { var result = await svc.RemoveFromWatchlistAsync(userId, ticker); return Results.Ok(result); }). Service method: public async Task<RemoveWatchlistResponse> RemoveFromWatchlistAsync(Guid userId, string ticker) { using var tx = await _db.BeginTransactionAsync(); var deleted = await _db.ExecuteAsync("DELETE FROM watchlist_items WHERE user_id = @userId AND ticker = @ticker", new { userId, ticker }); var alertsDeleted = await _db.ExecuteAsync("DELETE FROM price_alerts WHERE user_id = @userId AND ticker = @ticker", new { userId, ticker }); await tx.CommitAsync(); return new RemoveWatchlistResponse { Ticker = ticker, DeletedAlerts = alertsDeleted }; }
technical_notes.shared_types:
// File: packages/types/src/watchlist.ts
export interface RemoveWatchlistResponse { ticker: string; deletedAlerts: number; }
technical_notes.database: -- No schema changes. Uses existing watchlist_items and price_alerts tables. Cascade delete via transaction.

stories.title: Reorder watchlist items by drag-and-drop
stories.goal: organise my watchlist so the most important tickers are at the top
stories.benefit: so that I don't have to scroll to find the positions I'm actively managing
acceptanceCriteria: Given I am on the Watchlist tab, When I drag a row to a new position, Then the row moves to the new position and the order is persisted when I refresh the page
Given I reorder items, When I open the app on a second device, Then the same order is displayed

technical_notes.web_frontend: React component: <WatchlistTable />. Use @dnd-kit/core for drag-and-drop: import { DndContext, closestCenter, PointerSensor, useSensor, useSensors } from '@dnd-kit/core'; import { arrayMove, SortableContext, verticalListSortingStrategy } from '@dnd-kit/sortable'. Wrap table in <DndContext onDragEnd={handleDragEnd}><SortableContext items={watchlist} strategy={verticalListSortingStrategy}><WatchlistRow />... each row wrapped in useSortable hook. On drag end: compute new sort order (0, 1, 2, ...), update local state optimistically, debounce API call by 500ms using useDebounce hook. Mutation: useMutation({ mutationFn: (reorderedItems) => api.patch('/api/v1/watchlist/reorder', { items: reorderedItems.map((item, idx) => ({ ticker: item.ticker, sortOrder: idx })) }) });
technical_notes.web_backend: .NET Minimal API: app.MapPatch("/api/v1/watchlist/reorder", async (ReorderWatchlistRequest req, WatchlistService svc) => { await svc.ReorderWatchlistAsync(userId, req.Items); return Results.NoContent(); }). Service method: public async Task ReorderWatchlistAsync(Guid userId, List<WatchlistReorderItem> items) { // Validate ownership: ensure all tickers exist for this user var existing = await _db.QueryAsync<string>("SELECT ticker FROM watchlist_items WHERE user_id = @userId", new { userId }); var existingSet = existing.ToHashSet(); if (items.Any(i => !existingSet.Contains(i.Ticker))) throw new UnauthorizedAccessException("Cannot reorder tickers not in your watchlist"); // Bulk update using CASE WHEN for atomic transaction var sql = "UPDATE watchlist_items SET sort_order = CASE ticker " + string.Join(" ", items.Select((item, idx) => $"WHEN '{item.Ticker}' THEN {idx}")) + " END WHERE user_id = @userId"; await _db.ExecuteAsync(sql, new { userId }); }
technical_notes.database: -- No schema changes. Uses existing sort_order column in watchlist_items table.

features.title: Price Alert Creation & Delivery
features.description: Users can set price-crossing alerts on any watchlist item and receive timely push or email notifications when the threshold is met.

stories.title: Set a price alert on a ticker
stories.goal: set a notification for when a stock hits a specific price
stories.benefit: so that I know the right moment to place my order without watching the screen all day
acceptanceCriteria: Given I am on a ticker detail screen or watchlist row, When I click 'Set Alert', Then a dialog opens with fields: target price, direction (above/below), and notification channel (push/email)
Given I enter a valid target price and click 'Create Alert', When the request succeeds, Then a success confirmation is shown and the alert appears in my Alerts tab with status 'Active'
Given I already have 20 active alerts, When I click 'Create Alert', Then the creation is blocked with an inline message 'You've reached the 20-alert limit. Delete an alert to add a new one.'

Given I enter a target price that is already met (e.g. target $150 above, current price is $155), When I click 'Create Alert', Then an inline error 'AAPL is already above $150.00' is shown and the alert is not created

technical_notes.web_frontend: React component: <AlertCreationDialog ticker={ticker} currentPrice={currentPrice} />. Use Radix Dialog primitive. Form managed by React Hook Form + Zod schema: const schema = z.object({ targetPrice: z.number().positive(), direction: z.enum(['above', 'below']), channel: z.enum(['push', 'email']) }). Client-side validation: check if targetPrice is already met (if direction === 'above' && targetPrice < currentPrice, show error). Submit via TanStack Query mutation: useMutation({ mutationFn: (data) => api.post('/api/v1/alerts', data), onError: (err) => { if (err.status === 429) setError('You've reached the 20-alert limit.'); if (err.status === 422) setError(err.message); } }). On success: close dialog, invalidate ['alerts'] query, show toast 'Alert created for {ticker}'.
technical_notes.web_backend: .NET Minimal API: app.MapPost("/api/v1/alerts", async (CreateAlertRequest req, AlertService svc) => { var alert = await svc.CreateAlertAsync(userId, req); return Results.Created($"/api/v1/alerts/{alert.Id}", alert); }). Service method: public async Task<PriceAlert> CreateAlertAsync(Guid userId, CreateAlertRequest req) { // Check limit: var activeCount = await _db.ExecuteScalarAsync<int>("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM price_alerts WHERE user_id = @userId AND status = 'active'", new { userId }); if (activeCount >= 20) throw new TooManyRequestsException("20-alert limit reached"); // Validate not already met: var currentPrice = await _quoteCache.GetAsync(req.Ticker); if (req.Direction == "above" && req.TargetPrice < currentPrice.LastPrice) throw new ValidationException($"{req.Ticker} is already above ${req.TargetPrice:F2}"); if (req.Direction == "below" && req.TargetPrice > currentPrice.LastPrice) throw new ValidationException($"{req.Ticker} is already below ${req.TargetPrice:F2}"); // Insert: var alert = new PriceAlert { UserId = userId, Ticker = req.Ticker, TargetPrice = req.TargetPrice, Direction = req.Direction, NotificationChannel = req.Channel, Status = "active", CreatedAt = DateTime.UtcNow }; await _db.ExecuteAsync("INSERT INTO price_alerts (...) VALUES (...)", alert); return alert; }
technical_notes.database:
-- Migration: 20260611_add_price_alerts.sql
CREATE TABLE price_alerts (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  ticker TEXT NOT NULL,
  target_price DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
  direction TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(direction IN ('above','below')),
  notification_channel TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'push',
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK(status IN ('active','triggered','deleted')),
  triggered_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_alerts_active ON price_alerts(user_id, status) WHERE status = 'active';
CREATE INDEX idx_alerts_ticker ON price_alerts(ticker, status) WHERE status = 'active';

stories.title: Receive push notification when alert triggers
stories.goal: receive a timely notification when my price target is hit
stories.benefit: so that I can act on the opportunity before the price moves further
acceptanceCriteria: Given I have an active alert for AAPL at $150 above, When the price crosses $150, Then I receive a push notification within 60 seconds saying 'AAPL hit $150.00 — your alert triggered'
Given I receive a push notification, When I click it, Then the app opens to the ticker detail screen for that symbol
Given an alert triggers, When I view my Alerts tab, Then the alert status is changed to 'Triggered' with a timestamp

technical_notes.web_frontend: Service Worker: register Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) in public/firebase-messaging-sw.js. On app load: request notification permission via Notification.requestPermission(). If granted, call getToken() from Firebase SDK and send to backend via POST /api/v1/users/fcm-token. Listen for messages: messaging.onMessage((payload) => { new Notification(payload.notification.title, { body: payload.notification.body, data: { ticker: payload.data.ticker } }); }). On notification click: self.addEventListener('notificationclick', (event) => { event.waitUntil(clients.openWindow(`/ticker/${event.notification.data.ticker}`)); });
technical_notes.web_backend: Background worker: AlertEvaluationWorker runs every 5s. Query active alerts: SELECT * FROM price_alerts WHERE status = 'active'. For each alert, fetch current price from Redis. Evaluate: if (direction === 'above' && currentPrice >= targetPrice) || (direction === 'below' && currentPrice <= targetPrice) { trigger alert }. Update alert: UPDATE price_alerts SET status = 'triggered', triggered_at = now() WHERE id = @id. Send notification: await _fcmService.SendAsync(new FcmMessage { Token = user.FcmToken, Notification = new { Title = $"{alert.Ticker} hit ${alert.TargetPrice:F2}", Body = "Your alert triggered" }, Data = new { ticker = alert.Ticker } }). Use Firebase Admin SDK for .NET: FirebaseMessaging.DefaultInstance.SendAsync(message). Retry policy: 3 retries with exponential backoff (1s, 5s, 15s) if FCM returns 500.

outOfScope: Email notifications for alerts — Phase 2 (MVP is push-only)
Recurring alerts (alert re-activates after triggering) — Phase 2
Alert templates (save alert config for reuse) — Phase 3
Alert history (view past triggered alerts beyond 30 days) — Phase 2
